verdicts.note: Single article, but an explicit statement of support for the tax on income over $1M plus a stated principle that higher earners should pay a higher rate ('Let them pay their fair share') [S2]. The ESSB 6346 single-vote rule covers roll-call votes, not explicit statements; +2 at medium fits.

Single article, but S2 has two distinct pole_b statements: she opposes I-1 and says professionals, not outside direction, should decide what students learn. +2 at medium is consistent with one clear source.
Consistent with Payne +2: Kelso has never held public office but has held party office since 2020 and is on her third legislative run, so +1 rather than +2.
Rests on data-center siting and GMA reform. His school-related 'restore local control' line is correctly left to parental-rights under the addendum.
High is supported by his I-638 advocacy [S7][S2] plus his self-reported record: statewide girls'-sports proposals and the Mead board's Title IX pushback against OSPI [S7].

Consistent with Bingle -1: one local elective term (Mead board since 2023) plus county planning-commission and state code-advisory roles, with no legislative tenure. Record wording in the dossier is attributed as his claims ('says he helped'), which matches S7.

missing.basis: Says the Legislature has undercut law enforcement with recent laws [S3]; campaign site calls for 'consequences for criminal behavior' and addiction policies that do not 'enable it' [S5]. Pole_a, but only general statements with no enforcement specifics, so -1.
